segments.text: Hello Hannah, come and take a seat. What would you like to talk about today?
I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.
What happened in September?
It was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and I love it. And then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left...
That sounds like recognition of your work.
That's what everyone says but I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner
or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.
What does it look like when that dot arrives?
Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.
What do you rehearse?
Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong.
What do you imagine they would think?
That time out of my debt, that day you gave the job to a nice year-four teacher who can't actually read.
Has anyone said anything that's just that?
No, that's a strange thing. Nobody has. It's all in my head.
It's still very real to you?
Very. Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
Four times. What was the email about?
A change to the behavior policy. It was two paragraphs.
I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.
bit. How does he treat you? He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.
That makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him. Lying to him about what?
About being capable, as if I'm pretending.
Pretending to be what?
Somebody who knows what she's doing.
Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.
That's a bit of a match. Whose coat is that?
My mum's, I suppose. She was a headteacher for 20 years.
Tell me about that.
She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.
She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.
And you're now an assembly job?
I dip in this job, but yes, I can't help comparing.
Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?
Does she say that?
Never. She is very supportive on the surface.
She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.
How does it land when she says that?
It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss
So I don't tell her how bad it is
What does she not know?
That I'm awake at four every morning
I fall asleep fine
Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.
What's on the list?
Everything.
Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complained, a child I'm worried about.
It goes round and round.
How long have you been waking like that?
Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.
How many cups?
Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.
What do you notice in your body during those afternoons?
My heart goes fast.
My hands are a bit shaky. Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.
Did anyone notice?
I didn't think so. I said I was fetching a document.
That sounds like a lot of effort to hide it.
It is. I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending.
Who knows how you're feeling?
My partner Ben knows a bit. He says I should just enjoy it.
How do you feel when he says that?
Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.
You can't just fix this.
No. I wish it were that simple.
Do you have friends at school that can talk to you?
Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year for a quarter with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.
Say it was some company along with the promotion.
Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that. I miss them. I miss my class too.
What do you miss most?
The children mostly. Daily bit where a child gets something for the first time. No, my days are spreadsheets.
Do you want deeper motion?
I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.
The hat. Then I went home and cried.
Where did the tears evolve?
Here, I think. And that I would never get to go back.
Would you want to go back?
I don't know. It sounds terrible, doesn't it? After everything's been so supportive.
That sounds like an honest question.
Nobody has asked me that. They just say, well done.
When was the last time you felt properly relaxed?
These summer holidays we went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.
What was different there?
Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking. Ben carried the sandwiches.
Uh, yeah.
The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.
Is there anything you already tried to tell? Even let me?
I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A true laughing. A good email.
How did that go?
It held for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.
Silly in what way?
As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.
Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging.
Probably not. It just felt that way.
That sounds worth coming back to. Have you thought about whether there is something particular you would like from our world?
I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
What would that look like on a Tuesday?
Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first.
Sending an email once.
And on Sunday?
Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.
Those are clear goals.
How do you feel now, saying them out loud?
Tearful.
Lighter. A bit tearful actually.
That's alright. Take a moment.
Sorry, I didn't expect that.
There is nothing to apologize for. What's coming up?
That's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about before I am.
What would it be like to tell him?
Scary. It would probably be hard that I didn't say so.
Would it be a reason to keep it to yourself?
I suppose not
Try this week
Help you do that
If I choose a quiet moment
Not on a Sunday evening
Then I'm too wound up
Saturday morning, perhaps?
Yeah, over breakfast
He's always in a good mood then
And one more small thing. Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line?
I could. Well, put it by the kettle so I don't forget.
We're nearly out of time. Is there anything you want to add?
Why did I nearly cancel this morning? I'm glad I didn't.
I'm glad too. Same time next week?
Yes, please. Thank you.
